title: Revenue Cycle Rule — Billing Route for Immunization Services Doses
content:
Every Immunization Services dose is paid by exactly one billing route, chosen in the order below; the first route whose condition the patient meets is the route of the dose. The markers and figures named (Vaccines for Children stock and its highest age and administration fee, Medicare Part B and Part D markers, the zero cost-share marker, the cash price) are those of the vaccination in the product price schedule.

## R-1 Order of routes

1. **Vaccines for Children.** A child no older than the vaccination's highest age for Vaccines for Children stock who is uninsured or on Medicaid receives Vaccines for Children stock where the vaccination can be given from that stock. The billing route is the no-cost program, and the patient pays the vaccination's Vaccines for Children administration fee.
2. **Medicare.** A patient whose primary coverage is a Medicare class is billed to Medicare Part B where the vaccination is marked for Part B, with billing route medical benefit, or to the Part D plan on file where the vaccination is marked for Part D, with billing route pharmacy benefit.
3. **Other active coverage.** Any other patient with an active coverage record is billed to it, with billing route pharmacy benefit.
4. **Zero cost share.** Where the vaccination carries the zero cost-share marker and the patient meets the vaccine's recommendation, an insured dose costs the patient 0.00.
5. **Cash — no longer in force.** The former clause under which every other dose was paid in cash at the vaccination's cash price, less the savings program's vaccine discount where the patient holds an active Kestrel Rx Savings Club membership, rounded to the cent half up, is no longer in force; it is superseded by the current basis.

## R-2 Changing a course's billing route
A course's billing route is updated only for doses not yet given; a dose already given keeps the route it was paid by.

## Route selection at a glance

| Patient | Route |
|---|---|
| Child within the Vaccines for Children age, uninsured or on Medicaid, vaccination available from that stock | No-cost program, paying the administration fee |
| Primary coverage a Medicare class, vaccination marked for Part B | Medical benefit (Medicare Part B) |
| Primary coverage a Medicare class, vaccination marked for Part D | Pharmacy benefit (the Part D plan on file) |
| Any other patient with an active coverage record | Pharmacy benefit |

## Hypothetical cases

- A hypothetical 10-year-old on Medicaid receiving a vaccination available from Vaccines for Children stock up to age 18 takes the no-cost program route, ahead of any other route.
- A hypothetical Medicare patient receiving a vaccination marked for Part D is billed to the Part D plan on file under the pharmacy benefit route.
- A hypothetical course switched from one plan to another after dose 1 keeps dose 1 on the route it was paid by; only the doses not yet given move to the new route.

superseded_clauses: Every other dose is paid in cash at cash_price_usd, less the savings program's vaccine discount where the patient holds an active Kestrel Rx Savings Club membership, rounded to the cent half up.
